title: Joan of Arc and the Hundred Years' War
subject: histoire
description: In 1429, a 17-year-old peasant girl convinced the dauphin to entrust her with an army. In a few months, Joan of Arc reversed the course of a war that France seemed to have lost.

hero.hook: Seventeen years, one banner, and a kingdom that is rocking.

blocks.text: In **1429**, France seems lost. The English and their Burgundian allies hold the North. The dauphin Charles, heir to the throne, vegetated south of the Loire. It was then that a **17 year old** peasant woman, from Domrémy in Lorraine, claimed to have a divine mission.

**Joan of Arc** doesn't just transform the forehead. It changes the very legitimacy of the conflict. In his day, many believed in : the idea that God intervenes directly in history. Jeanne says she knows which of the two suitors He has chosen. [[Providentialism]]

The Hundred Years' War (1337-1453) opposed the kings of England (Plantagenêts) and the kings of France (Valois). In 1429, the country was also torn apart by a civil war: the [[Armagnacs]], loyal to the dauphin, against the [[The Burgundians]], allies of the English. The [[The Treaty of Troyes (1420)]] disinherited the dauphin in favor of the King of England. In Paris, Henry VI is proclaimed. Charles VII is nothing more than the “little king of Bourges”.

blocks.caption: Joan of Arc, figure of the French reconquest.

blocks.text: In **1428**, the English besieged **Orléans**, a key town on the Loire. If it falls, the south opens. It is in this despair that Jeanne leaves Lorraine.
Jeanne has never killed an enemy with her hand. She preferred to carry her banner rather than the sword, to lead without shedding blood herself.

Born around **1412**, Jeanne says she heard Saint Michael, Saint Catherine and Saint Marguerite from **13 years old**. Their order: lift the siege of Orléans, then lead the dauphin to . Only this rite, the anointing with holy oil in the cathedral of Reims, makes a true king in the eyes of the kingdom. [[coronation of Reims]]

In **February 1429**, in **Chinon**, on the Loire, she recognized Charles among his disguised courtiers. The theologians of Poitiers examined it for three weeks, then authorized it. He is given armor, a banner, and a convoy to Orléans.
In Poitiers, matrons checked her virginity. It was believed that a witch could not be a witch, because she would necessarily have made a carnal pact with the devil.

In **May 1429**, Jeanne broke a seven-month siege in **nine days**. The French troops are galvanizing. The English retreat. On **July 17**, Charles was crowned in Reims, in the heart of Burgundy. The Treaty of Troyes becomes politically obsolete: the king is anointed.

The momentum is running out of steam. Paris resists. On **May 23, 1430**, in Compiègne, Jeanne was captured by the Burgundians, then sold to the English for **10,000 pounds**. In Rouen, Bishop , a supporter of the English, orchestrates a heresy trial. On **May 30, 1431**, she was burned alive. [[Pierre Cauchon]]

blocks.text: Jeanne's death did not stop the reconquest. She united national sentiment around the throne. In **1456**, Charles VII had it rehabilitated. The war ends in , in Guyenne, in **1453**: the English are almost driven out of France. [[Castillon]]
Illiterate peasant, war leader, martyr, saint: Joan spans the centuries as a figure that each era reinvents. In a few months, she made possible what seemed lost.

In **1429**, Joan of Arc, **17 years old**, lifted the siege of Orléans and had Charles VII crowned. Burned in **1431**, rehabilitated in **1456**, it remains the symbol of a kingdom that refuses to disappear.
